1. Implement IMO-4:
   - Prepare IMO-4 using the following recipe:
     * 10 kg IMO-3
     * 5 kg field soil from your okra field
     * 5 kg red fine soil (from anthill or termite mound)
   - Mix these ingredients on the soil floor, creating a heap no more than 20 cm high.
   - Cover for two days and maintain moisture at 65-75% using natural farming inputs.
   - Apply IMO-4 to your okra field to improve soil fertility and microbial diversity.

2. Use Fish Amino Acid (FAA):
   - Prepare FAA using local fish waste and brown sugar.
   - Apply diluted FAA (1:1000 ratio) to your okra plants as a foliar spray and soil drench.
   - This will provide readily available nitrogen and other nutrients to your crops.

3. Implement cover cropping or intercropping:
   - Plant nitrogen-fixing legumes like cowpeas or mung beans between okra rows or as a cover crop during the off-season.
   - This will naturally increase soil nitrogen levels and improve soil structure.

4. Improve landscape connectivity:
   - Create diverse planting zones around your okra field using native plants.
   - Establish corridors of natural vegetation between fields to promote biodiversity and natural pest control.
   - This approach will enhance overall ecosystem health and resilience.

5. Continuous IMO application:
   - Collect and prepare IMOs annually from different parts of your land and surrounding areas.
   - This will maintain soil fertility and health over time.
